name: Alabama
analysis: Alabama's AV-specific statute governs automated commercial vehicles. Its scope does not establish a general passenger robotaxi pathway.
oversight: Alabama DOT has state-level jurisdiction under the commercial vehicle framework.

name: Alaska
framework: No enacted AV operation framework identified
analysis: Proposals to restrict autonomous operation and assign operator liability remained under consideration in the 2026 survey. Proposed bills are not current operating authority.
oversight: General motor vehicle law applies while the proposed AV measures remain unenacted.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Arizona
analysis: Arizona's AV framework grew from executive orders in 2015 and 2018. The state provides notification and certification guidance before testing and operation. A company operating in Arizona should not be interpreted as having statewide service coverage.
oversight: Arizona MVD notification and certification.
source_label: Arizona DOT AV framework and HB 2813 history

name: Arkansas
analysis: Arkansas permits driverless operation when statutory conditions and advance submissions, including commercial-purpose information, are satisfied.
oversight: State submission and applicable traffic and vehicle rules.

name: California
analysis: DMV regulates AV testing and deployment under Articles 3.7 and 3.8. Its 2026 update followed a draft, formal proposal and two modified comment rounds. CPUC separately authorizes passenger service: test pilots cannot charge fares, while deployment programs can. A DMV permit alone does not authorize paid rides.
oversight: DMV: vehicle testing, deployment permits and reporting. CPUC: passenger service pilots, fare-charging deployment, passenger safety and service reporting.

name: Colorado
framework: AV operating framework; truck restrictions vetoed
analysis: Colorado has an AV statute, while proposed in-vehicle human requirements for automated commercial trucks were vetoed in both 2025 and 2026. A vetoed bill cannot be treated as a current restriction.
oversight: State motor vehicle law and any applicable testing conditions.

name: Connecticut
analysis: Connecticut's dedicated AV pathway centers on a limited pilot involving selected municipalities. A pilot law is not blanket authority for commercial deployment statewide.
oversight: Pilot approval and participating municipalities.

name: Delaware
framework: No enacted AV-specific operating statute identified
analysis: Delaware's 2025 proposal to require an onboard operator failed. Its AV advisory activity does not itself grant a commercial permit.
oversight: Ordinary vehicle rules; no distinct statewide commercial AV permit identified in the guide.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Florida
analysis: Florida law allows driverless AV operation subject to statutory conditions. This review has not established a separate public company-level permit roster; a service announcement is not a state-issued ODD boundary.
oversight: Vehicle registration and statutory operating requirements.

name: Georgia
analysis: Georgia enacted rules for fully autonomous vehicles through SB 219. The Observatory has operating evidence, but has not located a public state holder roster; the statute and an operator's actual service geography answer different questions.
oversight: State motor vehicle law and applicable service regulation.

name: Hawaii
analysis: Act 21 (2020) established a state AV testing pilot with an onboard human driver and a report to the 2023 legislature. It did not grant broad driverless commercial authority.
oversight: Hawaii DOT determined eligible pilot testers.

name: Idaho
analysis: Idaho's executive-order committee examined testing and deployment issues. The 2026 survey identified no enacted AV-specific operating statute.
oversight: General motor vehicle requirements and agency guidance.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Illinois
analysis: Illinois law limits local governments' ability to prohibit AVs, but that rule alone does not establish a statewide permit or demonstrate an active commercial service.
oversight: State vehicle and traffic law; local powers are constrained by statute.

name: Indiana
framework: No enacted AV-specific operating statute identified
analysis: Indiana's 2025 bill addressing autonomous tractor-trailers failed. The 2026 survey did not identify a dedicated AV operating law.
oversight: Ordinary vehicle and commercial-carrier requirements.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Iowa
analysis: Iowa's statute addresses operation of automated driving systems. Multiple proposed 2026 changes failed, so those proposals should not be counted as current conditions.
oversight: State traffic and vehicle requirements under Iowa's AV statute.

name: Kansas
analysis: Kansas law accommodates private and commercial AV operation subject to statutory conditions. This permission says nothing about a particular company's ODD.
oversight: State vehicle and traffic rules.

name: Kentucky
analysis: Kentucky's AV framework took effect in 2024. The survey reports that a temporary onboard-driver rule for very heavy commercial vehicles expired in August 2026 after an extension failed.
oversight: State vehicle law and any remaining commercial-carrier requirements.

name: Louisiana
analysis: Louisiana's dedicated AV operating provisions focus on commercial uses. Passenger service cannot be inferred from that freight-oriented authority.
oversight: State commercial-vehicle and traffic requirements.

name: Maine
analysis: Maine authorizes transportation officials to establish AV pilot activity. The guide does not describe a broad commercial robotaxi approval regime.
oversight: Maine DOT pilot rules and general vehicle requirements.

name: Maryland
analysis: Maryland's AV-specific statute focuses on converted vehicles for commercial or industrial use. Broader 2025 operation and safety-operator bills did not pass.
oversight: Motor Vehicle Administration and applicable vehicle law.

name: Massachusetts
analysis: Executive Order 572 established a testing framework in 2016 and was rescinded by Executive Order 603 in 2022. Current testing authority needs separate verification.
oversight: Do not rely on the rescinded order for current testing.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Michigan
analysis: Michigan law covers research, testing and operation and permits driverless use under statutory conditions, including minimal-risk capability and insurance. SAVE projects have separate manufacturer limits.
oversight: State AV statutes and vehicle rules.

name: Minnesota
framework: No comprehensive AV operation law enacted
analysis: Minnesota proposed an AV and on-demand network framework in 2026, but it failed. The proposal should not be represented as an active permit system.
oversight: General vehicle rules and any relevant agency guidance.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Mississippi
analysis: Mississippi allows a person to operate an AV when statutory conditions are met. The permission is broader than a manufacturer-only test program.
oversight: State traffic, registration, and safety requirements.

name: Missouri
analysis: A Missouri proposal requiring an active human driver was still pending in the survey. Its introduction alone does not change current AV operating law.
oversight: General state motor vehicle and carrier rules.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Montana
analysis: Montana enacted measures addressing automated vehicles and platooning in 2025. The exact authority for a proposed passenger or freight service requires examination of the relevant provisions.
oversight: State vehicle and commercial-carrier requirements.

name: Nebraska
analysis: Nebraska permits ADS-equipped vehicles with an onboard licensed driver and provides a conditional pathway for operation without one.
oversight: State statutory requirements for driverless operation and ordinary vehicle law.

name: Nevada
analysis: Nevada provides separate DMV applications for autonomous-vehicle testing and certification for operation. No complete public list of current holders was found in the sources reviewed.
oversight: Nevada DMV testing and operation certification.

name: New Hampshire
analysis: New Hampshire provides a testing pilot and an AV advisory commission. Those provisions do not establish general commercial deployment statewide.
oversight: Pilot approval and commission reporting.

name: New Jersey
analysis: A 2026 bill proposed a fully autonomous vehicle pilot. The guide identifies it as pending, so a proposed pilot cannot be shown as active authorization.
oversight: General motor vehicle rules pending enacted AV legislation.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: New Mexico
analysis: New Mexico's AV framework addresses testing and requires advance notification. A testing notice is distinct from commercial deployment approval.
oversight: State transportation and testing-notification requirements.

name: New York
framework: State demonstration permit; additional NYC test permit
analysis: Testing in New York City requires a New York State DMV demonstration or testing permit and a separate NYC DOT permit. A NYC testing permit does not authorize commercial passenger service.
oversight: NYS DMV demonstration program; NYC DOT testing permit within the city.
source_label: New York State DMV AV demonstration

name: North Carolina
analysis: North Carolina has AV-specific operating provisions and a committee charged with recommendations for testing and deployment. A statewide law does not reveal a company's actual service area.
oversight: State traffic law and committee-led policy review.

name: North Dakota
analysis: North Dakota permits autonomous operation subject to applicable state and federal law. A 2025 AV funding proposal failed.
oversight: Ordinary vehicle law plus the state's AV operating provision.

name: Ohio
analysis: Ohio's DriveOhio program requires companies to register before AV testing. The guide identifies no general AV operation statute; registration should not be read as commercial deployment approval.
oversight: DriveOhio testing registration and state vehicle rules.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Oklahoma
analysis: Oklahoma permits AV operation when statutory conditions and ordinary registration rules are satisfied; on-demand networks also remain subject to applicable service law.
oversight: State traffic, registration, and on-demand network requirements.

name: Oregon
framework: Task force, no general operating law
analysis: Oregon established an AV task force. A 2026 proposal to permit operation without ordinary driving privileges failed.
oversight: General vehicle law while broader AV operation proposals remain unenacted.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Pennsylvania
analysis: Pennsylvania's AV pathway places oversight with PennDOT and requires self-certification. A separate 2025 certificate proposal was pending in the survey.
oversight: PennDOT self-certification and state traffic requirements.

name: Rhode Island
framework: No dedicated AV operating law identified
analysis: The 2026 survey identifies no AV-specific statute or new proposal. That does not establish that an individual deployment is authorized.
oversight: General motor vehicle and service rules.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: South Carolina
framework: No dedicated AV operating law identified
analysis: South Carolina's survey entry identifies no new AV legislation since 2018. Operator status still depends on general vehicle law and any service-specific rules.
oversight: General state motor vehicle requirements.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: South Dakota
analysis: South Dakota added an AV operating statute in 2024 alongside earlier platooning provisions. Commercial freight and passenger services should be assessed under their relevant requirements.
oversight: State AV, commercial-carrier, and traffic rules.

name: Tennessee
analysis: Tennessee has a general AV operating framework. A 2026 amendment addresses traffic violations committed by AVs, adding a distinct accountability issue to the state's policy picture.
oversight: State traffic law and the Automated Vehicles Act.

name: Texas
analysis: Texas authorized AV operation in 2017 and added a mandatory TxDMV authorization for commercial automated-vehicle operation in 2026. The state does not publish a complete public holder roster in the sources reviewed; documented service is distinct from authorization.
oversight: TxDMV commercial authorization; traffic-law and insurance requirements.

name: Utah
analysis: Utah's AV law governs operation of ADS-equipped vehicles subject to state and federal requirements. A 2026 information-request bill failed.
oversight: State AV statute and ordinary traffic requirements.

name: Vermont
analysis: Vermont's AV law addresses testing only, with public comment and an onboard human driver for each approved test. It is not a general driverless passenger-service pathway.
oversight: Test-specific approval and public-comment process.

name: Virginia
analysis: Virginia considered autonomous operation licenses in SB 670, but the measure was continued to 2027 in the survey. Its proposed licenses are not existing permits.
oversight: General vehicle law pending any enacted AV-specific licensing framework.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Washington
analysis: Washington distinguishes eligibility to test AVs on public roads from registration of the vehicle itself. Neither alone identifies an operating service area.
oversight: State testing self-certification and vehicle registration processes.

name: West Virginia
analysis: West Virginia's AV law accommodates several service types subject to conditions. Driverless operators must submit a law-enforcement interaction plan before operating.
oversight: State vehicle rules and law-enforcement interaction plan.
source_label: West Virginia Fully Autonomous Vehicle Act

name: Wisconsin
analysis: Wisconsin's AV steering committee addressed testing and deployment policy. Proposed 2026 board and permit legislation failed, leaving no such new permit in force.
oversight: General vehicle rules and existing agency coordination.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: Wyoming
analysis: The 2026 guide identifies no AV-specific operating law or new proposal in Wyoming. That finding does not amount to a positive authorization for any proposed service.
oversight: General motor vehicle and commercial-carrier rules.
source_label: State law survey (secondary source; verify primary text)

name: District of Columbia
analysis: District rules address AV testing with a human behind the wheel; a testing provision is not commercial deployment authorization.
oversight: DDOT oversight.
source_label: DDOT AV law and testing guidance
